slots_and_copies.name: flash_object_store
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Wear-leveled object/sector allocator over 16 x 0x1000-byte sectors (confirmed via FUN_0801ab60/FUN_0801b150/FUN_0801b3a8 sector-count bounds of 0x10). No evidence of a fixed primary/backup whole-save mirror; redundancy, if any, is per-object relocation on write, not pinned down statically.

checksums.name: record_header_sum8_complement
checksums.formula_detail: byte[+0x06] = (sum of bytes in [_DAT_0801aef8 .. _DAT_0801aef8+_DAT_0801aef4]) mod 256; byte[+0x07] = 0xFF - byte[+0x06] (ones'-complement guard). Covered byte range is runtime-resolved and could NOT be statically reproduced; only the mechanism and header offsets are confirmed.

checksums.name: record_header_complement_guard_byte
checksums.formula_detail: byte[+0x07] is the exact ones'-complement of byte[+0x06]: byte[+0x07] == 0xFF - byte[+0x06]. Independently verified against the real .sav file regardless of the unresolved checksum range.

io_driver_functions.notes: Flash chip-ID read: AA/5555, 55/2AAA, 90/5555 ID-entry sequence, reads 2 ID bytes, then AA/55/F0 ID-exit/reset.
Device-table lookup by chip ID; copies geometry/command descriptor fields out of the matched device-table entry.
Generic byte-swap/copy staging helper used by the chip-ID and erase routines.
Bank-addressed burst program path (no erase issued); forwards to unresolved func_0x0807bf1c.
Bank-addressed read-back/verify path; forwards to unresolved func_0x0807bf1c and returns its result.
4KB sector erase: AA/55/80, AA/55, then 0x30 (SST-style Sector Erase) at bank-addressed target; bounded to 16 sectors (param_1 < 0x10).
Generic unsigned 32-bit integer divide (math utility, not save-specific; used somewhere in save offset/size arithmetic).

fuzzing_targets.mutation: increment byte 0x01->0x02 at 0xF04C without touching the checksum pair
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If inside the checksum's covered range, save is flagged corrupt on reload; if outside, loads normally with the mutated byte's own (unknown) effect visible — used to binary-search the checksum's covered range.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: recompute sum8+complement over each of the top candidate covered ranges and patch 0xF006/0xF007 accordingly after mutating a payload byte
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Only the repair using the true covered range reloads cleanly; this is the decisive experiment to pin down checksum coverage.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: change 0x09 to 0x00 or 0xFF, leave checksum pair untouched
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If validated independently of the checksum, save is rejected/ignored despite an internally consistent sum/complement pair.
If a displayed label, visible change on load/select screen; if an internal format tag, save may be rejected.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: flip one 0x00 byte to 0xFF inside the FF FF FF 00 stride pattern at 0xF420-0xF52F
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If this is an allocated-object bitmap, a previously valid slot may disappear from an in-game list (e.g. mission/profile selection).

fuzzing_targets.mutation: zero the entire high-entropy tail block at 0xF530-0xF56A
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If independently checksummed, expect a corruption/fallback response; if cosmetic, expect normal load with at most a visual anomaly.
If a real end-of-store sentinel, directory-scan behavior changes (store treated as freshly erased); if incidental, no change.

What does the FF FF FF 00 striped region at 0xF420-0xF52F represent?
What is the high-entropy tail block at 0xF530-0xF56A, and is it itself checksummed?
Is the 00 55 pair at 0xFFFE-0xFFFF meaningful or incidental?

What are the concrete SWI numbers behind func_0x0807bf10/14/18/1c (believed to be BIOS CpuSet/CpuFastSet-family wrappers based on sibling functions in the same address range, but not directly observed)?
